title: Chiral rotational dynamics in the molecular frame: Breaking symmetry with angular momentum
authors: Alexander Blech, Monika Leibscher, Christiane P. Koch
abstract: Achiral molecules can be prepared in superposition states that are chiral. Here, we propose angular momentum orientation in the molecular frame to achieve the required symmetry breaking, exerting rotational control without the need for laboratory frame orientation. We derive the conditions for chiral rotational dynamics from the requirement to simultaneously break the continuous spatial rotational symmetry and the molecular point group symmetry. This can be achieved by three microwave pulses as well as two non-resonant optical pulses in combination with a THz pulse or three THz pulses, all with mutually orthogonal polarization directions, and the ensuing dynamics can be probed by photoelectron circular dichroism. Our results open the way for distinguishing structural from dynamical enantioselectivity and investigating time-odd chiroptical phenomena in randomly oriented molecules.
summary: This paper proposes a method to generate rotational chirality in achiral molecules by manipulating their angular momentum using precisely timed microwave or THz/optical pulse sequences. By satisfying strict symmetry breaking conditions, the induced chirality can be measured using Photoelectron Circular Dichroism. This opens a new avenue for studying time-odd chiroptical phenomena in fundamental molecular systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of generating and investigating time-odd (false) chirality in isolated, achiral molecules by controlling their rotational dynamics.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that rotational chirality can be induced in randomly oriented molecules using specific sequences of microwave or combined THz/optical pulses, which can be probed via Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD).
method: The theoretical framework involves deriving symmetry conditions for creating chiral superpositions of rotational states, while the experimental proposals utilize pulsed laser/microwave excitation sequences.
model_or_system: The system studied is the rigid asymmetric rotor (e.g., $	ext{CH}_2	ext{O}$, $	ext{COFCl}$), whose dynamics are governed by the time-dependent Schrödinger equation under external pulsed fields.
key_observables: The expectation value of the angular momentum projection ($\langle \hat{J}_z angle$) and the Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) signal are the key diagnostics for induced chirality.
important_parameters: The required excitation involves at least three microwave or polarization directions (X, Y, Z) to break both spatial and molecular point group symmetries.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the rigid rotor approximation and that the probe pulse is short compared to the rotational dynamics timescale.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the excitation schemes (microwave/THz/optical) and show the time evolution of the induced angular momentum ($\langle \hat{J}_a angle$) and the corresponding PECD signal, demonstrating controllable handedness.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the problem (time-odd chirality) to deriving the necessary symmetry conditions for state superposition, detailing specific pulse sequences for microwave and optical excitation, and finally presenting PECD as the measurable diagnostic.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it tackles the fundamental control of molecular quantum states using tailored electromagnetic pulses, pushing the boundaries of chiroptical spectroscopy in the gas phase.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. A rotating achiral molecule, here CH2O, becomes dynamically chiral: The sense of rotation reverses upon re- flection, breaking the molecule’s mirror symmetry. Handed- ness can be assigned via the convention of the thumb oriented along the molecular symmetry axis (dashed arrow), and the fingers represent the sense of rotation encoded in the angular momentum component Jz (solid arrow).

FIG. 2. Rotational chirality induced in an achiral asymmetric rotor, here COFCl, by a sequence of three microwave pulses, polarized along three mutually orthogonal directions. (a) Rotor spectrum and excitation scheme with initial state (black dot) and final superposition (red ellipses). (b) Population dynamics (accumulated over M). (c) Expectation value of the angular momentum component along the a-axis, quantifying the induced chirality, as well as LPECD as obtained after one-photon ionization with an ultrashort XUV pulse. The microwave pulses are indicated in gray.

FIG. 3. Rotational chirality induced in a thermal ensemble of achiral asymmetric rotors, here CH2O at a temperature of 5 K, by THz and optical pulses (gray shadings) with mutually orthogonal polarization directions: (a,b) combination of a THz pulse with two femtosecond optical pulses; (c,d) three THz pulses. (a,c) Angular momentum components along the laboratory Z-axis, signaling unidirectional rotation, and along the molecular a-axis, quantifying the induced chirality. (b,d) LPECD signal assuming instantaneous ionization.
